kanjiDisposition.reason: Actual labels and every raw English meaning identify plants, animals, shapes, mystery/apparition, objects, numbers/ranks, a field boundary or lack. Secondary clock-hand, mallet/spine, hard-drinker and calendar senses were included. None supplies an imperial order or a sovereign's words.

Receiving/enjoying/undergoing, congealing/absorption, strength, overcoming/kindness/skill, medicine, associate rank, recompense, redundancy, blades, clergy, imitation, salary, risking/assuming a name, exemption/dismissal, smelting and colleagues/officials are distinct from an imperial order. An edict can appoint, exempt or affect an official, but its possible subject, recipient or consequence is not its meaning.

Criminal punishment/sentencing and censure/criminal investigation concern punitive or investigative acts, not any sovereign's directive. A decree may concern punishment, but that relationship does not make these displayed answers interchangeable.

The three curated labels are bundle, efficacy/effectiveness and employment/diligence. Full raw 束 also preserves govern/manage/control; that broader action is not itself an imperial order. Merit/benefit and serving do not change the other two labels into directives. Source820's full applicable lexical-family inspection remains inherited, not claimed freshly repeated here.

Full raw character record gives imperial order; actual Daijisen character/noun headings separately support sovereign's words/orders and imperial association. The noun heading's additional尊貴command sense remains visible in the source; no absolute claim that every possible use is a Japanese constitutional edict. Two declared direct guards令/命 are unchanged.

wordDisposition.reason: Complete families and actual bodies identify an ancient chancellor/Chinese-style minister title, government official, prefectural governor and consul. These are people/offices, not an edict. The secondary Chinese-style minister sense of丞相 was considered, not dismissed solely as ancient-China vocabulary.

Offices/agencies/authorities, prefectural administration/premises, government/administration/ministry and a capital/metropolis are institutions or places, not their orders. Related government tags do not establish substitutable translations in either meaning direction.

Medieval and modern times, origin/primeval state and civilization/culture or the Bunmei era name do not name an edict. Full secondary periodization, beginning and proper-era senses were inspected. An edict can belong to one of these settings without meaning that setting.

Autocracy/despotism, self-government/local autonomy, official/public business and taxes/duties are different from an imperial edict. Arbitrary control may be exercised through edicts, public work can implement them and an edict can impose tax; none of those relations makes the displayed label an alternative definition of the target.

Wrongdoing/illegality/fraud, scolding/reprimanding, the actualたまbullet identity and a Japanese sword do not name an edict. Complete弾families retain ball/jewel/coin and the separateだんcounter senses; spelling preferences and actual primary reading were considered, not an invented exclusive-kanji compartment. None creates target ambiguity.

Complete1430550 gives imperial edict; actual Daijisen separates sovereign/king orders from the particular Meiji constitutional legal form. Label imperial edict and reverse勅令(ちょくれい) fit both. Six conservative direct word guards remain unchanged; no inferred vocabulary level.
